name: Solvang Drift Parka
description:
Solvang is a Scandinavian-heritage outdoor brand that's been operating in the Great Lakes corridor for decades, selling gear to people who actually spend time outside in the region's serious winters. The Drift Parka is their cold-weather workhorse — a mid-thigh length shell in a matte ripstop with a down-analog synthetic fill, the hood oversized enough to accommodate a helmet or a heavy hat and still close around the face. The design is deliberately understated: two colors, glacier white and a dark navy, no visible branding beyond a small embossed logo at the chest zip. The insulation runs to the wrists and the fill weight is serious enough that below-zero temperatures feel like a negotiation rather than a defeat.

This is a Tier 3 to Tier 4 purchase — expensive enough that Tier 2 buyers make it a significant investment, cheap enough that it's not a status item in the Spire. Wilderness guides, researchers who work at the lake-monitoring stations, and people who commute via elevated walkways in January all wear it. It has none of the tech features of its more expensive competitors and doesn't need them. It is simply a very good parka.
what_it_says: You respect the weather. You've been outside when it got serious.
worn_by: Tier 4 buyers who want function over status
story_hooks: A researcher found something at the lake monitoring station she wasn't supposed to find, and the only record of her being there is a glacier-white parka on a security camera she didn't know about.
The Solvang warehouse doubles as a meeting point for a mutual aid network that operates in the outer Tier 2 zones; the parka has become an informal identifier.
A Tier 4 buyer paid resale for a parka that still has the previous owner's name written in marker on the interior tag — a name that appears on a missing persons list.
